==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂welh₁-|id=rule}}
From {{inh|en|enm|valew}}, {{m|enm|value}}, from {{der|en|fro|value}}, feminine past participle of {{m|fro|valoir}}, from {{der|en|la|valeō|valēre|be strong, be worth}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*walēō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂welh₁-||to be strong}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|văl'ū}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈvæl.juː/|a=RP}} (but cf. ''valu<u>able</u>'' {{IPAchar|/ˈvæljəbəl/}}).
* {{IPA|en|/ˈval.jʉw/|a=SSB}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈvæl.ju/|a=US,CA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-value.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈvæl.jʉː/|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈvɛl.jʉː/|a=NZ}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈval.jʉ/|a=Scotland,NI}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈvalɪʊ/|a=Wales}}
* {{hyph|en|val|ue}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# The [[quality]] that renders something desirable or [[valuable]]; [[worth]].
#: {{syn|en|worth|Thesaurus:value}}
#: {{ux|en|There is tremendous '''value''' in a good education.}}
#: {{ux|en|An abacus is of little '''value''' when you have an electronic calculator.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=May 13, 2012|author=Alistair Magowan|work=BBC Sport
|title=[http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/17973162 Sunderland 0-1 Man Utd]
|passage=United were '''value''' for their win and Rooney could have had a hat-trick before half-time, with {{w|Paul Scholes}} also striking the post in the second half.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The [[degree]] of [[importance]] given to something.
#: {{ux|en|The '''value''' of my children's happiness is second only to that of my wife.}}
# {{lb|en|often plural}} That which is valued or highly [[esteem]]ed, such as one's [[moral]]s, morality, or [[belief system]].
#: {{co|en|family '''values'''}}
#: {{ux|en|He does not share his parents' '''values'''.}}
# The [[amount]] (of [[money]] or [[goods]] or [[services]]) that is considered to be a fair [[equivalent]] for something else.
#: {{ux|en|The '''value''' of the stolen painting is estimated to be around four million pounds.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1825|author=w:John Ramsay McCulloch|title=Principles of Political Economy
|passage=An article may be possessed of the highest degree of utility, or power to minister to our wants and enjoyments, and may be universally made use of, without possessing exchangeable '''value'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Du Fresnoy Dryden Painting|passage=His design was not to pay him the '''value''' of his pictures, because they were above any price.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-03|volume=408|issue=8847| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21582498-america-has-changed-way-it-measures-gdp-boundary-problems Boundary problems]| passage=Economics is a messy discipline: too fluid to be a science, too rigorous to be an art. Perhaps it is fitting that economists’ most-used metric, gross domestic product (GDP), is a tangle too. GDP measures the total '''value''' of output in an economic territory. Its apparent simplicity explains why it is scrutinised down to tenths of a percentage point every month.}}
# {{lb|en|music}} The relative [[duration]] of a musical note.
#: {{ux|en|The '''value''' of a [[crotchet]] is twice that of a [[quaver]].}}
# {{lb|en|arts}} The relative [[darkness]] or [[lightness]] of a color in (a specific area of) a [[painting]] etc.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Edith Anderson Feisner|title=Colour: How to Use Colour in Art and Design
|passage=When pigments of equal '''value''' are mixed together, the resulting color will be a darker '''value'''. This is the result of subtraction.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2010|author=Rose Edin; Dee Jepsen|title=Color Harmonies: Paint Watercolors Filled with Light
|passage=Shadows and light move very quickly when you are painting on location. Use Cobalt Blue to quickly establish the painting's values.}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics|physics}} Any definite [[numerical]] [[quantity]] or other mathematical [[object]], determined by being measured, [[compute]]d, or otherwise [[define]]d.
#: {{ux|en|The exact '''value''' of [[pi]] cannot be represented in [[decimal]] notation.}}
# Precise [[meaning]]; [[import]].
#: {{ux|en|the '''value''' of a word; the '''value''' of a legal instrument}}
#* {{RQ:Mitford Greece|passage=Yet that learned and diligent annotator has , in a following note , shown his sense of the '''value''' of a passage of Livy , marking , in a few words , most strongly the desolation of Italy under the Roman republic}}
# {{lb|en|in the plural}} The valuable [[ingredient]]s to be obtained by treating a [[mass]] or [[compound]]; specifically, the [[precious metal]]s contained in rock, gravel, etc.
#: {{ux|en|The vein carries good '''values'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|the '''values''' on the hanging walls}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Esteem; [[regard]].
#* {{RQ:Dryden Fables|Preface|passage=The French have a high '''value''' for them ; and I confess they are often what they call delicate}}
#* {{RQ:Burnet History
|passage=My relation to the person was so near, and my '''value''' for him so great.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[valour|Valour]].
#: {{alti|en|valew<l:obsolete>}}
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=II|canto=VI|page=264|passage=Who ſoone prepard to field, his ſword forth drew, / And him with equall '''valew''' counteruayld: {{...}}}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# To [[determine]] or [[estimate]] the value of; to judge the [[worth]] of.
#: {{syn|en|appreciate|assess|evaluate|valuate|worthen|Thesaurus:appraise}}
#: {{ant|en|misappraise|undervalue}}
#: {{ux|en|I will have the family jewels '''valued''' by a professional.}}
#: {{ux|en|The property has been '''valued''' at six million pounds.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-03|volume=408|issue=8847
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21582498-america-has-changed-way-it-measures-gdp-boundary-problems Boundary problems]
|passage=Economics is a messy discipline: too fluid to be a science, too rigorous to be an art. Perhaps it is fitting that economists’ most-used metric, gross domestic product (GDP), is a tangle too.{{...}}But as a foundation for analysis it is highly subjective: it rests on difficult decisions about what counts as a territory, what counts as output and how to '''value''' it. Indeed, economists are still tweaking it.}}
# To [[regard]] [[highly]]; [[think]] [[much]] of; place [[importance]] upon.
#: {{syn|en|esteem|honor|look up to|respect|Thesaurus:revere}}
#: {{ant|en|despise|disesteem|Thesaurus:despise}}
#: {{ux|en|Gold was '''valued''' highly among the Romans.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''value''' his advice.}}
# To [[hold dear]]; to [[cherish]].
#: {{syn|en|treasure|prize|Thesaurus:hold dear}}
#: {{ant|en|despise}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''value''' these old photographs.}}
